keys.name: APERTURE_ORIGIN
keys.description: Browser origin allowed to call this API in addition to WEB_ORIGIN.

keys.name: AUTH_ENABLE_DEV_LOGIN
keys.description: Enables the "Developer sign-in" shortcut on /signin (dev only).

keys.name: BACKUP_S3_URI
keys.description: ── Off-box backups (scripts/backup-to-s3.sh; see docs/runbooks/restore-drill.md) S3 URI prefix for automated full exports (includeSensitive). IAM least privilege on …/exports/* only. Prefer GHA OIDC or an EC2 instance role; no keys in git.

keys.name: BACKUP_SSE_KMS_KEY_ID
keys.description: Uploads are server-side encrypted (SSE-S3/AES256) by default; set a KMS CMK to use SSE-KMS instead. IAM must allow kms:GenerateDataKey/Decrypt on the key.

keys.name: BUILDSVC_HMAC_SECRET
keys.description: Shared secret for HMAC-SHA256 request signing (SRS T4). Must match buildsvc. This secret IS the compiler's authentication. buildsvc refuses to start without it and rejects the published development defaults in production. node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('hex'))"

keys.name: BUILDSVC_URL
keys.description: LaTeX build service (SRS §8.4)

keys.name: CLOUDINARY_FOLDER
keys.description: Folder prefix for all Vitae uploads.

keys.name: CLOUDINARY_URL
keys.description: Storage: Cloudinary (SRS T5)

keys.name: DATABASE_CA_CERT
keys.description: PEM bundle for verifying the database's TLS certificate. Required whenever DATABASE_URL is not localhost: RDS certificates are signed by an Amazon CA that Node does not trust by default, and the alternative to supplying it is `rejectUnauthorized: false`, which accepts any certificate at all.

keys.name: DATABASE_POOL_MAX
keys.description: Single-user workload; a large pool would only hold RDS connections idle.

keys.name: DATABASE_URL
keys.description: Postgres, the data plane (ADR 0005). The default points at the local compose service; production supplies the RDS endpoint and is refused at boot if it is still carrying this default (see assertSafeCombination).

keys.name: DOCS_CONTENT_DIR
keys.description: Where the compiled documentation corpus lives on disk. The corpus is served by this API rather than by the public web host, because it is private: it describes the whole system, and its generated half enumerates every route, endpoint, table and exported symbol in the repository. Behind this API it inherits the OWNER_EMAIL allow-list that gates every other request, which is the only reason it is readable at all. Unset means no corpus was built into this deployment, and the endpoints report that rather than pretending the documentation is empty.

keys.name: FIREBASE_AUTH_EMULATOR_HOST
keys.description: When set, the Admin SDK talks to the local Auth emulator instead of prod.

keys.name: FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID
keys.description: Firebase: AUTH ONLY (ADR 0005). Sign-in stayed on Firebase when the data plane moved to Postgres, because `verifyIdToken` is free, unmetered, and was never the constraint. There is no Firestore here any more.

keys.name: GITHUB_PAT
keys.description: Third-party credentials come from the deployment's secret manager, never from application data (FR-004). Optional: the file-backed secret store in `.secrets/` backs local/self-hosted installs.

keys.name: OWNER_EMAIL
keys.description: Auth (SRS INT-1 / FR-SET-001)

keys.name: PADDLE_ENVIRONMENT
keys.description: Paddle server credentials and server-owned price IDs. Put these only in the deployment secret manager, never in a VITE_ variable or committed .env file.

keys.name: PUBLIC_APP_URL
keys.description: Canonical browser origin used by provider return links and account messaging.

keys.name: SESSION_SECRET
constraints: min(16, SESSION_SECRET must be at least 16 chars)
keys.description: 32+ byte random string used to sign dev-login session tokens.

keys.name: TRUSTED_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID
keys.description: A second Firebase project whose ID tokens are also accepted: the companion app (Aperture) signs in the same human against its own project, and a Firebase token is scoped to the project that issued it. This widens which identity provider can prove "I am the owner"; it does not widen *who* the owner is. The OWNER_EMAIL check still gates every request, and the cross-project path additionally demands a verified email from a Google sign-in. Unset = the feature is off.

keys.name: VITAE_CLOUD_ENABLED
keys.description: Keep false for every self-hosted installation. Enable only with the complete launch checklist in docs/CLOUD-LAUNCH.md and a tested staging lifecycle.

keys.name: VITAE_SECRETS_DIR
keys.description: Where the file-backed secret store lives (default: <repo root>/.secrets).

keys.name: VITE_API_BASE_URL
keys.description: Public base URL of the API, consumed by the web app at build time.

keys.name: VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY
keys.description: Web SDK config (emulator-safe placeholders are fine for local dev).

keys.name: VITE_FIREBASE_AUTH_EMULATOR_HOST
keys.description: Where the Web SDK reaches the Auth emulator when USE_EMULATOR is true. The emulator serves its own Google account chooser, so "Continue with Google" works locally. Sign in as OWNER_EMAIL or the API's owner check rejects you.

keys.name: VITE_PADDLE_CLIENT_TOKEN
keys.description: Public Paddle client token, scoped to checkout only. Never use an API key here.

keys.name: VITE_PUBLIC_CLOUD_ENABLED
keys.description: The marketing site stays pre-launch and unindexed unless every public legal value below is explicitly configured. These are public identifiers, never billing keys or provider secrets. The API has a separate, stricter release gate for provisioning and billing.

keys.name: VITE_PUBLIC_REPOSITORY_URL
keys.description: Optional canonical source link for the public site. When omitted, the site uses a neutral GitHub source-discovery query and publishes no maintainer ID.

keys.name: WEB_ORIGIN
keys.description: Comma-separated browser origins allowed by CORS (primary web + aliases).
